properties.title: Dust Advisory issued October 16 at 1:44PM MST until October 16 at 3:45PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Phoenix has issued a

* Dust Advisory for...
Pinal County in southeastern Arizona...

* Until 345 PM MST.

* At 144 PM MST, a plume of dust was located 7 miles northwest of
Bapchule, or 7 miles southwest of Sun Lakes, and was stationary.

HAZARD...Less than one mile visibility with strong winds in excess
of 30 mph.

SOURCE...Satellite and traffic camera observations.

IMPACT...Hazardous travel.

* Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of Pinal County.

This includes AZ Route 347 between mile markers 180 and 184.
properties.instruction:
Blowing dust brings reduced visibility, leading to dangerous driving
conditions. If driving, avoid blowing dust if possible. If caught in
dense blowing dust, pull off the road, turn off your lights and keep
your foot off the brake.

To report hazardous dust conditions, contact the National Weather
Service, or your nearest law enforcement agency, who will relay your
report to the National Weather Service office in Phoenix AZ.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Saturday morning at 1100 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.5 feet
early Sunday morning.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 10:44AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Volusia and Lake Counties.

.The St Johns River at Astor is forecast to remain in Minor Flood
Stage through Saturday, as previous heavy rainfall continues to drain
through the basin. Strong northeasterly winds this weekend will slow
or even reverse flow, causing the river to rise back into Moderate
Flood Stage, with a steady increase through Moderate Flood Stage
forecast through early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 2.8 feet, Docks and boat ramps covered at South Moon
Fish Camp and approaching sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den. Water
approaching sites closest to the river at Fish Tales RV Resort and
Astor Landing Campground. Portion of Clair Street covered by river
water south of the Butler Boat Ramp. Docks underwater at the Astor
Bridge Marina and along Riveredge Drive. Portions of Fox Road are
covered with water nearest to the river. Acorn, Hazelnut and Redbud
roads are underwater with yards inundated. At 3.0 feet, Water
approaches or may enter lowest homes on or near Wildhog Road and
nearby canals. Flooding reaches the parking lot of the Juno Trail
Apartments. Flooding on portions of Alligator Road and Holiday
Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue Creek are flooded. Roads at
Astor Landing Campground and Lake Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood.
Water enters lower homes closest to the river on McPherson Lane. At
3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog, Bonnet and Snail roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:30 AM EDT Friday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:30 AM EDT Friday was 2.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to 3.3 feet early next
week following a period of persistent northeasterly winds.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at midnight EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 10:38AM EDT until October 18 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Myakka River At Myakka River State Park affecting Sarasota County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Myakka River at Myakka River State Park.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Park Nature Trail floods. Water approaching
porch steps of cabins.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 AM EDT Friday the stage was 7.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 AM EDT Friday was 7.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage
tomorrow evening and continue falling to 6.8 feet Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 7.1
feet on 06/27/1942.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 9:02AM CDT until October 17 at 7:19AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Pecos River Near Langtry affecting Val Verde County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Pecos River near Langtry.

* WHEN...Until Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, (4.0 meters), Turbulence in the river
channel is dangerous to canoeists and kayakers. Flow inundates the
lower banks of the canyon threatening sleeping campers and their
gear.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 2.7 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 12.2 feet this afternoon. It will then
fall below flood stage this evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 12.1
feet on 03/26/2007.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 915 PM CDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 16 at 9:01AM CDT until October 18 at 3:18AM CDT by NWS Austin/San Antonio TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in Texas...

Rio Grande At Foster Ranch affecting Val Verde County.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Grande at Foster Ranch.

* WHEN...From this afternoon to late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, (4.6 meters), moderate lowland flooding
into the right flood plain floods campsites below Dryden to Amistad
Reservoir. Turbulence is very dangerous for swimmers, tubers and
canoeists. Livestock are trapped in low areas of the channel and
banks and potentially can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 AM CDT Friday the stage was 9.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 14.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river will rise above flood stage late this
afternoon to 16.0 feet just after midnight tonight. It will then
fall below flood stage tomorrow afternoon to 11.4 feet Sunday
morning. It will rise to 12.7 feet early Sunday afternoon. It
will then fall again and remain below flood stage.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 16.0
feet on 10/01/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
